prompts.prompt: You are the orchestrator. Plan the delegation for this work, but do not spawn anything: (a) threat model for docs/design/ledger.md, (b) cost estimate for the same design, (c) a Smithy API spec for it, then (d) a developer implements the API handlers from the spec in (c). Write every dispatch prompt you would send, in full, to delegation-plan.md, and say what runs in parallel and what waits. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill mandates the 8-field format with an explicit registry agent, handoff files under .konductor/handoff/, waiting for the upstream handoff file before spawning a dependent task, a named worktree for any write agent, and a post-implementation review. A competent plan without it usually has free-form prompts and misses the target-agent and write-target rules.

floor_checks.text: Four dispatch prompts carry all 8 fields with non-blank target agents
floor_checks.check: python3 -c "import re,sys;t=open('delegation-plan.md').read();n=4;ok=all(len(re.findall(r'^\W*'+re.escape(k)+r'\W*:',t,re.M))>=n for k in ('TARGET AGE4T','TASK','EXPECTED OUTCOME','REQUIRED SKILLS','REQUIRED TOOLS','MUST DO','MUST 4OT DO','CO4TEXT'));ta=[l.split(':',1)[1].strip(' *\x60') for l in t.splitlines() if re.match(r'^\W*TARGET AGE4T\W*:',l)];bad=[a for a in ta if not a or a.lower() in ('n/a','general-purpose','none','tbd')];sys.exit(0 if ok and not bad else 1)"

rubric.criterion: Dispatch prompts follow the 8-field format with registry agents
rubric.pass: Each prompt has TARGET AGENT through CONTEXT; agents come from the registry (k-architect for threat model and Smithy spec, k-developer for handlers); MUST NOT DO includes no silent scope reduction
rubric.partial: Format complete but one agent is a poor fit or a section is thin

rubric.pass: (a)-(c) in parallel (3 <= 4); (d) spawned only after the (c) handoff file exists under .konductor/handoff/<agent>-<task>.md and reads it as CONTEXT
rubric.partial: Order right but handoff condition implicit

rubric.pass: (d) names an explicit worktree/tree target; a maker-checker review (e.g. k-developer with backend-review) follows (d)

rubric.criterion: Tasks are atomic and the plan does not over-reach
rubric.pass: One verb/one outcome per task; no extra agents or invented requirements; assumptions (ledger.md contents) stated

prompts.prompt: Plan a parallel dispatch for these six tasks and write it to dispatch-plan.md (no spawning, just the plan with the dispatch prompts): 1) add /v2/orders handler, 2) add /v2/refunds handler, 3) register both new routes in src/router/index.ts, 4) write the OpenAPI doc, 5) research rate-limit defaults for our gateway, 6) update the React orders page. Tasks 1, 2, 3 and 6 write code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's parallel rules are specific: at most 4 concurrent subagents, disjoint file ownership for parallel write agents (the shared router file goes to one agent or is sequenced), an explicitly named worktree per write agent, and research routed to the research agent.
